traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md are satisfied. Core functionality is implemented via AnnotationRuleOptions, resolveOptions, and resolvePattern to support both nested (story/req) and flat (storyPathPattern/requirementIdPattern) configuration. Backward compatibility is preserved using default regex patterns and examples when options are missing or invalid, with resolvePattern falling back on errors. Pattern validation is done by constructing RegExp inside a try/catch and recording configuration errors, which valid-annotation-format surfaces through the invalidRuleConfiguration message while continuing validation using defaults. Error messages use configurable storyPathExample/requirementIdExample (and nested story.example/req.example), with tests confirming these appear in diagnostics and that nested values override flat ones. JSON Schema for all options is provided by getRuleSchema and wired into the rule meta.schema, following ESLint configuration best practices. Integration consistency with valid-story-reference is maintained by aligning the default story path pattern with that rule’s default storyDirectories (docs/stories, stories). Tests comprehensively cover configuration, regex validation, error messaging, fallback behavior, and nested-vs-flat precedence, and they pass under the project’s Jest test run. Therefore, the story is fully implemented and verified.
